questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The opportunity to study at one of the best universities in the US and experience a highly dedicated and engaging study environment -- both in terms of professors and students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Exceeded all expectations. Large network of international students who are easy to get in touch with and very helpful faculty members at the Department of Sociology.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yale has been particularly helpful and quick to respond to emails etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My advisor and the Office for International Students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy finding housing opportunities off-campus via Facebook pages.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Walking distance from campus is a big plus -- East Rock is a good and lively neighborhood in New Haven.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I quickly got in touch with my supervisor who guided me to choose the right courses for me from the course catalog. YaleHub allows you to register for different courses, but it's a good idea to reach out to the professor/teacher via email beforehand to secure a spot.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My advisor, other students, and the Yale administration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try all the courses you can in the first week and then sign up for the ones you like best.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: PhD-oriented. Very different but I learned a lot!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: PhD-oriented seminars.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Seminars for 7-15 graduate students enrolled in a Ph.D. program at Yale. Discussion-based learning.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Mixed Methods Research, Feminist and Queer Theories, Decolonizing Thought, Stratification and Inequality
Workshop.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Graduate Level courses in general - better match for MA level at the UCPH.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Choose courses that a not offered by UCPH and check out the professor's teaching style beforehand. Take advantage of the close relationship possible to develop with other students in your field and the professors (since the teaching style is small seminars). See as many theater performances by Yale as possible, they are amazing!
